chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The earth is folded up at the end of the night.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the earth is folded up at the end of the night?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the 'folding' of the earth at the end of the night serves as a metaphor for the transient nature of worldly existence and the ease with which Allah can alter creation. Shia scholars often link this to the concept of *Qabd* (contraction) as a precursor to *Bast* (expansion) on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing divine omnipotence over physical reality. This imagery reinforces the believer's detachment from the material world by viewing daily cycles as microcosmic signs of eschatological events.

en.hubeali: H 14939 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammaad Bin Usman, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said:
‘The earth folds up during the end of the night’.
en.sarwar: 492. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazaz who said: We intended to go out, so we went to greet Abu Abdullah (a.s.). So he (a.s.) said: ‘It is as if you all are seeking blessings for Monday’. So we said, ‘Yes’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘So which day is greater in evil than the day of Monday, the day in which our Prophet (saww) departed, and the Revelation was Raised (stopped) from us (a.s.). Do not go out, and go out on the day of Wednesday’.
